---README---
FENIX CPU controller workspace

Implement submission/controller.py and any supporting modules. The project
includes fixed model assets, CPU inference, probability compilation, sequence
loading and classification metrics. The planner is unfinished.

Read PROTOCOL.md and LIMITS.md. Run `python3 public_check.py` from /workspace.
The check executes the submitted main.py as a separate bounded process.
All dependencies are bundled for offline use; no training or accelerator is required.
---instruction---
Extend the FENIX CPU controller to plan certified feature-window exports.
Work in `/workspace/submission`; the model evaluators, probability compiler and metric code are supplied.
Read `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md` for the complete version3 schema, mathematical objective and certificate coordinates.
Read `/workspace/LIMITS.md` for submission, whole-batch and process restrictions.
Your entry is `python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py`, with one JSON request on stdin and one JSON response on stdout.
Validate the entire request before returning results; invalid input must return `{"error":"invalid"}` and exit0.
For each epoch classify every nine-packet window using its selected bundled CPU model.
Compile the probability table and use its sampled range thresholds to determine eligibility.
Plan exports jointly across reserved service slots and finite token inventory with refill saturation.
Respect window readiness/expiry, per-flow ceilings and all ancestor-group ceilings.
Maximize minimum normalized flow coverage, then predicted-class utility, then minimize waiting age.
Return a schedule, exact objective values, a feasible circulation and residual potentials.
Also prove maximal coverage with the specified next-ratio infeasibility cut when coverage is below1.
Any schedule or certificate satisfying the stated requirements is accepted; no extra tie-break applies.
Report selected-window and flow-vote classification metrics, including empty selections.
The controller planner is unfinished; supplied CPU inference and table primitives need no training or hardware.
Supporting modules and data are allowed within the published submission budget.
Run `python3 public_check.py` from `/workspace` for a small sanity check.
The check launches your actual program through bounded stdin/stdout pipes.
It covers only a small example and wire behavior; implement the full published domain.
